newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher on weather talk.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher on weather talk.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly higher Friday with some talk of possible warm temperatures in the Southwest pulling Palo Verde (PV) prices higher, industry sources said.

"With (natural) gas moving higher I think that pulled electricity along behind it, and there was some strength in the PV prompt months with talk of firmer weather and that brought COB (California Oregon Border) up as well," said one futures broker.
NYMEX natural gas futures rose Friday, with some talk of shortcovering and possible technical tests of resistance levels before an expected move downward next week, sources said.
November PV futures settled up 30 cents at $16.25 after trade as high as $16.35, while December climbed 10 cents to $17.05 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Most remaining deferreds ended between five cents higher and five cents lower.
November COB rose 15 cents to $17.10 after reaching to $17.45, while December closed up 13 cents at $18.40.
Remaining COB deferreds settled mostly up 10 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 207 COB and 69 PV contracts traded Friday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
